questions.question: The tops of two buildings, 90 m and 55 m high, are connected by a metal wire. If the metal wire makes an angle with the horizontal, and tan θ = 3/7, then what is the distance (in metres) between the two buildings? (estimated)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in heights of the buildings = 90 − 55 = 35 m.

From the right-angled triangle formed, tan θ = Height Difference ÷ Distance.

⇒ Distance = Height Difference ÷ tan θ

⇒ Distance = 35 ÷ (3/7) = (35 × 7) ÷ 3 = 245 ÷ 3

⇒ Distance ≈ 81.66 m, which is estimated to 82 meter.

**∴ The correct answer is 82 meter.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of taller building = 90 m

Height of shorter building = 55 m

Angle of the metal wire with the horizontal = θ

tan θ = 3/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b777197f9ca7eadee90f166ade232dc197fff3efd1a1a89ae08d30f293ea98d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculation:**

⇒ Difference in height (Perpendicular) = 90 − 55 = 35 m

⇒ Let the horizontal distance between the buildings be 'd'.

⇒ In the right-angled triangle formed, tan θ = 35 ÷ d

⇒ 3/7 = 35 ÷ d

⇒ 3 × d = 35 × 7

⇒ 3d = 245

⇒ d = 245 ÷ 3

⇒ d ≈ 81.66 m

⇒ The estimated distance is 82 meter.

**∴ The correct answer is 82 meter.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object located above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios

For any right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base, sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, and cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².
</p

questions.question: A boat takes 28 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and coming back to point C midway between A and B. If the velocity of the stream is 6 km/h, and the speed of the boat in still water is 9 km/h, what is the distance between A and B?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Downstream Speed** = 9 + 6 = 15 km/h; **Upstream Speed** = 9 − 6 = 3 km/h.

Let total distance **AB** = x km. Then distance **BC** = x/2 km.

Total time = Time(**A→B**) + Time(**B→C**) = x/15 + (x/2)/3 = 28 hours.

x/15 + x/6 = 28 ⇒ (2x + 5x)/30 = 28 ⇒ 7x/30 = 28.

x = (28 × 30) ÷ 7 = 120 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in **Still Water** (u) = 9 km/h

Speed of **Stream** (v) = 6 km/h

Total time taken for the trip = 28 hours

**Formula Used:**

**Downstream Speed** (Sd) = u + v

**Upstream Speed** (Sᵤ) = u − v

**Time** = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84a67fb8665afb3d4102475ea7ba727b226bb749cb981d12a67b7d3964d5791f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Downstream Speed** = 9 + 6 = 15 km/h

⇒ **Upstream Speed** = 9 − 6 = 3 km/h

⇒ Let distance **AB** = D km. Since **C** is the **midway** point, **BC** = D/2 km.

⇒ Time for **A to B** (Downstream) = D/15 hours

⇒ Time for **B to C** (Upstream) = (D/2) ÷ 3 = D/6 hours

⇒ Total Time = D/15 + D/6 = 28

⇒ (2D + 5D) ÷ 30 = 28

⇒ 7D/30 = 28

⇒ D = (28 × 30) ÷ 7

⇒ D = 4 × 30 = 120 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Basics

The speed of a boat in the direction of the stream is Sd = u + v, and against the stream is Sᵤ = u − v, where u is speed in **Still Water** and v is **Stream Velocity**.

Speed in Still Water from Sd and Sᵤ

The speed of the boat in **Still Water** can be calculated as u = (Sd + Sᵤ) ÷ 2.

Stream Velocity from Sd and Sᵤ

The velocity of the **Stream** can be calculated as v = (Sd − Sᵤ) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: If Radha starts from A with a speed of 30 km/h and Shyam starts from B with a speed of x km/h they meet at C. After the meeting, they reach each other's starting point in 4 hours and 9 hours respectively. Find the speed of Shyam.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects meet and take time T₁ and T₂ to reach their opposite destinations:

Speed Ratio (S₁ ÷ S₂) = √(T₂ ÷ T₁)

⇒ 30 ÷ x = √(9 ÷ 4)

⇒ 30 ÷ x = 3 ÷ 2

⇒ 3x = 60 ⇒ x = 20 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Radha (S₁) = 30 km/h

Speed of Shyam (S₂) = x km/h

Time taken by Radha to reach B after meeting at C (T₁) = 4 hours

Time taken by Shyam to reach A after meeting at C (T₂) = 9 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86f486b202d8165216a73f2def49c00da38813c3b6eb6c3d1a74dcab7cd0a869.png] 

**Formula Used:**

When two moving bodies travel towards each other, cross a meeting point, and then take T₁ and T₂ hours respectively to reach their final destinations:

⇒ S₁ ÷ S₂ = √(T₂ ÷ T₁)

**Calculation:**

⇒ 30 ÷ x = √(9 ÷ 4)

⇒ 30 ÷ x = 3 ÷ 2

By cross-multiplying:

⇒ 3 × x = 30 × 2

⇒ 3x = 60

⇒ x = 20 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SRₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds: SRₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Average Speed

If an object covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).
</p

questions.question: The radius and the height of a right circular cone are in the ratio 3 ∶ 4. If its volume is 301.44 m3, find the slant height (use π = 3.14).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of radius to height is 3 : 4, which means the right-angled triangle formed by r, h, and l is a 3-4-5 triplet.

Let radius (r) = 3x, height (h) = 4x, and slant height (l) = 5x.

Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × h ⇒ (1/3) × 3.14 × (3x)² × 4x = 301.44

⇒ 37.68 × x³ = 301.44 ⇒ x³ = 8 ⇒ x = 2 m

Slant height (l) = 5x = 5 × 2 = 10 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of radius (r) and height (h) = 3 : 4

Volume of the cone = 301.44 m

questions.question: The ratio of volume of two cylinders H₁ and H₂ is sqrt{2} ∶ sqrt{3} respectively. If the ratio of height of the two cylinders H₁ and H₂ is 4 ∶ 9, then what is the ratio of the curved surface area of H₁ and H₂ respectively?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a cylinder, CSA² = 4π²r²h² = 4π(πr²h)h = 4π(V × h), which gives a direct relation: CSA ∝ √(V × h).

⇒ CSA₁ / CSA₂ = √(V₁h₁ / V₂h₂)

⇒ Ratio = √[(√2 / √3) × (4 / 9)]

⇒ Ratio = √[(2¹/² × 2²) / (3¹/² × 3²)] = √(2⁵/² / 3⁵/²)

**∴ The correct answer is 2⁵/⁴ : 3⁵/⁴.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] <span

questions.question: There are three numbers, the 1st number is thrice the 2nd and the 3rd number is three-fourth of the 1st. If the average of the three numbers is 125, the 2nd largest number is?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The 1st number is thrice the 2nd and the 3rd number is three-fourth of the 1st.

**Concept used: **

Sum of N numbers = Average × N

**Calculation:**

Let's assume that the 2nd number is = x,

Then, according to the question, 1st number is = 3x and the 3rd number is = 3x times (3)/(4) = (9x)/(4) now,

⇒ x+3x+(9x)/(4) = 125 times 3 

⇒ (4x+12x+9x)/(4) = 125 times 3 

⇒ 25x= 125times 3times 4 

⇒ x = 60 

Now, the 2nd largest number is (9)/(4)times 60 = 135 

**∴ The correct answer is 135**

questions.question: The ratio in which the line segment joining (5, -4) and (-3, 2) is divided by x-axis is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio** in which the **x-axis** divides the line segment joining (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by −y₁ : y₂.

Given points are (5, −4) and (−3, 2). Here y₁ = −4 and y₂ = 2.

Required **ratio** = −(−4) : 2 = 4 : 2 = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ∶ 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Points A(5, −4) and B(−3, 2).

**Formula Used:** **Section Formula** for y-coordinate: y = (m₁y₂ + m₂y₁) / (m₁ + m₂). On the **x-axis**, the **y-coordinate** of any point is always **0**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc0ce07e7a89fa139d7d728b0c82b5934905315cfc300590e4b7dd74af45502d.png] 

Let the **x-axis** divide the segment AB in the ratio **k : 1** at point P(x, 0).

⇒ 0 = [k × 2 + 1 × (−4)] / (k + 1)

⇒ 0 × (k + 1) = 2k − 4

⇒ 0 = 2k − 4

⇒ 2k = 4

⇒ k = 4 / 2 = 2

⇒ Ratio = k : 1 = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ∶ 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division by Y-axis

The ratio in which the **y-axis** divides the segment joining (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is −x₁ : x₂.

Internal Section Formula

For a segment divided in ratio m : n, the coordinates of the point are ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)).

Mid-point Formula

If the ratio is 1 : 1, the point is ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).

questions.question: Two trains 250 m and 300 m long are running on parallel rails in the same direction at speeds of 80 km/h and 65 km/h, respectively. Time taken by the faster train to cross the slower train will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Lengths of two trains = 250m and 300m

Speeds of two trains = 80km/h and 65km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed of same direction = S₁ - S₂

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

Relative speed of same direction = S1 - S₂ 

⇒ 80 - 65 = 15 km/h 

⇒ 15 x (5 / 18) = 25 / 6 m/s

Total distance covered by the two train = 250m + 300m = 550 m

Time taken by the faster train to cross the slower train will be

Time = Distance / Relative Speed 

⇒ 550 / (25 / 6) = (550 * 6) / 25 = 132 s

**Hence, The time taken by the faster train to cross the slower train will be 132 seconds**

questions.question: The radius of a solid metallic sphere is equal to 15 cm. It is melted and drawn into a long wire of radius 15 mm having uniform cross-section. Find the length of the wire.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of melted Sphere = Volume of cylindrical Wire ⇒ L = Volume of sphere ÷ Area of cross-section.

Radius of wire (r) = 15 mm = 1.5 cm.

L = (4/3 × π × R³) ÷ (π × r²)

L = (4/3 × 15³) ÷ 1.5² = 4500 ÷ 2.25 = 2000 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2000 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of solid metallic sphere (R) = 15 cm

Radius of wire (r) = 15 mm = 1.5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Sphere = 4/3 × π × R³

Volume of Cylinder (Wire) = π × r² × L

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8892c46072172945a09617046f096f2d63cee3bdcdbb890154c2f2e077de8214.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since the sphere is melted to form the uniform wire, their volumes must be equal.

⇒ Volume of Sphere = Volume of Wire

⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = π × r² × L

⇒ 4/3 × 15³ = 1.5² × L

⇒ 4/3 × 3375 = 2.25 × L

⇒ 4500 = 2.25 × L

⇒ L = 4500 ÷ 2.25

⇒ L = 2000 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2000 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conservation of Volume

Whenever a solid metallic object is melted and recast into another geometric form, the total volume remains strictly constant assuming no material is lost in the process.

Volume of a Cylinder

A wire is typically considered a very long cylinder. The volume of a solid cylinder of radius r and length (or height) h is given by V = π × r² × h.

Volume of a Sphere

The total internal volume of a solid 3D sphere of given radius R is calculated using the formula V = 4/3 × π × R³.

Units Conversion

It is essential to convert all physical measurements to a common consistent unit before substituting them into equations. For linear length, 1 cm = 10 mm.
</p

**Given:**

ΔABC,

OA = 12 cm, OC = 15 cm

∠AOB = ∠BOC = ∠COA

∠BAC = 60°

**Concept used:**

Concept of similarity

**Calculation:**

If ∠AOB = ∠BOC = ∠COA., then all the angles are 120° [Complete angle = 360°]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ea76df9f4ecb126d2685c5dcb537852315360380657e285dbeb334bfa3b8c91.png] 

In ΔOAC

Let ∠OAC be θ

∠OCA = 60° - θ [sum of angles of triangle is 180°]

In ΔAOB

∠OBA = θ [sum of angles of triangle is 180°]

From the above calculation, we can say

ΔOAB ∼ ΔOCA [AAA Similarity]

So,

OA/OC = OB/OA

⇒ 12/15 = OB/12

⇒ OB = 12² ÷ 15

⇒ OB = 144 ÷ 15

questions.question: One-third of a natural number is 56 more than one-fifth of 125. Find the square root of the required natural number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

One-fifth of 125 = 125 ÷ 5 = 25

One-third of the required number = 25 + 56 = 81

The required natural number = 81 × 3 = 243

Square root of the number = √243 = 9√3

**∴ The correct answer is 9√3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One-third of a natural number is 56 more than one-fifth of 125.

**Method Used:**

Form a linear equation and simplify using basic arithmetic operations to find the unknown value, then calculate its square root.

**Calculations:**

Let the required natural number be x.

⇒ x / 3 = (125 / 5) + 56

⇒ x / 3 = 25 + 56

⇒ x / 3 = 81

⇒ x = 81 × 3

⇒ x = 243

We need to find the square root of the required natural number:

⇒ √x = √243

⇒ √x = √(81 × 3)

⇒ √x = 9√3

**∴ The correct answer is 9√3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Used to solve arithmetic expressions in the order of Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Surds Simplification

To simplify a square root, separate the number into a perfect square and another factor: √(a² × b) = a√b.

Linear Equations

An algebraic equation where the highest power of the variable is 1. It is solved by performing inverse operations to isolate the variable.
</p

questions.question: If 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0, then one of the values of x - (1)/({2x)} is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide the equation 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0 by 2x to find x + 1/(2x) = −5/2.

Use the direct relationship (x − 1/2x)² = (x + 1/2x)² − 2.

Calculation: (−5/2)² − 2 = 25/4 − 2 = 17/4.

Taking square root: x − 1/2x = √17 / 2.

**∴ The correct answer is √17 / 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0

**Formula Used:** (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

⇒ 2x² + 1 = −5x

⇒ (2x² + 1) / 2x = −5x / 2x

⇒ x + 1/(2x) = −5/2

Now, to find x − 1/(2x), square both sides of the identity:

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = (x + 1/(2x))² − 4 × x × (1/2x)

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = (−5/2)² − 2

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = 25/4 − 2

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = (25 − 8) / 4 = 17 / 4

⇒ x − 1/(2x) = ±√(17 / 4)

⇒ x − 1/(2x) = √17 / 2 (taking positive value)

**∴ The correct answer is √17 / 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Reciprocals

For any value k, if x + 1/x = k, then (x − 1/x)² = k² − 4.

Quadratic Formula

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a.

Square of a Sum and Difference

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab is a fundamental identity used to convert between sums and differences.</p

questions.question: The sum of and difference between the LCM and HCF of two numbers are 512 and 496, respectively. If one number is 72, then the other number is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (512 + 496) ÷ 2 = 504

HCF = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (512 − 496) ÷ 2 = 8

Property: Product of Numbers = LCM × HCF

72 × Second Number = 504 × 8

Second Number = (504 × 8) ÷ 72 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of LCM and HCF = 512

Difference of LCM and HCF = 496

First Number (N₁) = 72

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19a4b05d72770be6f43beabd5fcfc10e46ed6e082a5ac6a41f18457fa5575123.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let LCM be L and HCF be H.

⇒ L + H = 512 --- (i)

⇒ L − H = 496 --- (ii)

⇒ Adding (i) and (ii): 2L = 1008 ⇒ L = 504

⇒ Subtracting (ii) from (i): 2H = 16 ⇒ H = 8

⇒ N₁ × N₂ = L × H

⇒ 72 × N₂ = 504 × 8

⇒ N₂ = (504 × 8) ÷ 72

⇒ N₂ = 4032 ÷ 72 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Numbers and their LCM/HCF

The product of any two numbers is always equal to the product of their LCM and HCF. Formula: N₁ × N₂ = LCM × HCF.

HCF as a Factor

The HCF of any group of numbers is always a factor of their LCM. This means LCM ÷ HCF will always result in an integer.

HCF of Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. In such cases, their LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.</p

questions.question: The cost of a shirt is 20% less than the cost of a trouser. The cost of 3 shirts and 5 trousers is ₹1,260 more than the cost of 5 shirts and 2 trousers. What is the cost of 4 shirts and 3 trousers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the cost of a Shirt (S) to a Trouser (T) = 80 : 100 = 4 : 5.

Cost difference = (3S + 5T) − (5S + 2T) = 37 units − 30 units = 7 units.

7 units = ₹1,260 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹180.

Required cost = 4S + 3T = 4 × 4 + 3 × 5 = 31 units = 31 × 180 = ₹5,580.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The cost of a shirt is 20% less than the cost of a trouser.

The difference between the cost of (3 shirts + 5 trousers) and (5 shirts + 2 trousers) is ₹1,260.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/847bd4546562f93e23547fa2783e9b958f97f9638bf7e8ff880d9cd2f4aeca10.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost of a trouser (T) be 5x.

⇒ The cost of a shirt (S) is 20% less = 5x − (20/100 × 5x) = 4x.

⇒ Cost of 3 shirts and 5 trousers = 3(4x) + 5(5x) = 12x + 25x = 37x.

⇒ Cost of 5 shirts and 2 trousers = 5(4x) + 2(5x) = 20x + 10x = 30x.

⇒ Given difference = 37x − 30x = 7x.

⇒ 7x = 1,260 ⇒ x = 1,260 ÷ 7 = 180.

⇒ We need to find the cost of 4 shirts and 3 trousers.

⇒ Required cost = 4(4x) + 3(5x) = 16x + 15x = 31x.

⇒ Required cost = 31 × 180 = 5,580.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio & Proportion Basics

When one quantity is given as a percentage of another, converting the percentage directly to a ratio simplifies calculations. For example, 20% less means 80% or 4/5 of the base value.

Linear Equations Setup

Word problems often translate into linear equations. Assigning variables to a common multiplier (like 4x and 5x) prevents fractions and maintains integer relationships.

Unitary Method

Finding the value of 1 base unit first (x = 180) allows easily calculating the value of any other required combination simply by multiplying the unit factor with the target equation.

questions.question: A pump can fill a tank with water in 2 hours. Because of a leak, it takes 6 hours to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water from the tank in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a pump fills a tank in x hours and with a leak takes y hours, the time taken by the leak to empty the tank is given by:

Time = (x × y) ÷ (y − x)

Here, x = 2 hours and y = 6 hours.

Time = (2 × 6) ÷ (6 − 2) = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pump to fill the tank = 2 hours

Time taken by Pump + Leak to fill the tank = 6 hours

**Method Used:**

We use the LCM method to find the total capacity of the tank and the efficiency of the pump and the leak.

 
 

 **Component**
 **Time (hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pump
 2
 6
 6 ÷ 2 = 3
 
 

 Pump + Leak
 6
 6 ÷ 6 = 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Pump + Efficiency of Leak = Combined Efficiency

⇒ 3 + Efficiency of Leak = 1

⇒ Efficiency of Leak = 1 − 3 = −2 units/hour

⇒ The negative sign indicates that the leak is emptying the tank at a rate of 2 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken by the leak to empty the full tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Time = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (doing positive work), whereas an outlet pipe or a leak empties it (doing negative work).

Pipes & Cisterns Formula

If a pipe fills a tank in A hours and another empties it in B hours (where B > A), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1 ÷ A − 1 ÷ B).

Combined Work Efficiency

Combined efficiency is the algebraic sum of the individual efficiencies: ETₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ − E₃ (where E₃ represents an emptying pipe or leak).

questions.question: A seller sells a laptop to Seema at the rate of Rs. 38,804 earning a 9% profit. He sells 2 mobile phones to Arjun, each at the rate of Rs. 13,875 earning a profit of 11% each. What is the total profit he earned on selling a laptop and 2 phones?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two mobile phones sold to Arjun at a profit of 11% each and rate of 13,875.

He also sells a laptop to seema at the rate of Rs. 38804 earning a 9% profit.

Formula used:

Profit or Gain = Selling price – Cost Price

Loss = Cost Price – Selling Price

Profit percentage = (Profit /Cost Price) x 100

Loss percentage = (Loss / Cost price) x 100

Calculations:

According to question,

If 109% of CP of laptop is equivalent to 38,804

Then, 9% of CP (i.e., profit) is equivalent to 38,804 × 9/109 = 3204

Similarly, if 111 % of mobile phone is equivalent to 13,875

Then, 11% is equivalent to 13,875 × 11/111 = 1375

Total profit

= profit on laptop+ 2 × profit on mobile 

= 3204 + 2(1375)

= 3204 + 2750

= Rs.5954

∴ The selling price of a second mobile phone is Rs. 5954.

questions.question: The number of students in a class is 45, out of which 33(1)/(3)% are boys and the rest are girls. The average score of girls in Science is 66(2)/(3)% more than that of boys. If the average score of all the students is 78, then the average score of girls is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Boys : Girls = 33(1/3)% : 66(2/3)% = 1 : 2

Ratio of Average Scores (B : G) = 100 : 166(2/3) = 3 : 5

Weighted average = [(1 × 3) + (2 × 5)] ÷ (1 + 2) = 13/3 units

13/3 units = 78 ⇒ 1 unit = (78 × 3) ÷ 13 = 18

Average score of girls = 5 units = 5 × 18 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total students = 45, Boys % = 33(1/3)%, Overall average = 78.

**Formula:** Average = Total Score ÷ Number of Students

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a74bd77c28b7da3e50fb51d68eec085ee6c6add6a579998f7f2ba31a9ff5cf9.png] 

⇒ Number of boys = 45 × (1/3) = 15

⇒ Number of girls = 45 − 15 = 30

⇒ Ratio of B : G = 15 : 30 = 1 : 2

⇒ Let boys' average = 3x, then girls' average = 3x + (2/3 × 3x) = 5x

⇒ Total score = (1 × 3x) + (2 × 5x) = 13x

⇒ Combined Average = 13x ÷ 3 = 78

⇒ 13x = 78 × 3 = 234

⇒ x = 234 ÷ 13 = 18

⇒ Average score of girls = 5x = 5 × 18 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

Weighted Avg = (n₁ × a₁ + n₂ × a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is quantity and a is average.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

33(1/3)% = 1/3 and 66(2/3)% = 2/3. Using these fractions simplifies complex calculations significantly.

Alligation Method for Averages

The ratio of the quantities is inversely proportional to the deviations of their averages from the mean average.</p

Two trains A and B leave Delhi for Hyderabad at 7 : 00 a.m. and 7 : 50 a.m. on the same day and travel at 80 kmph and 100 kmph respectively. After how many kilometers from Delhi will the two trains be together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train A speed = 80 km/h

Train B speed = 100 km/h

Train A departure time = 7:00 a.m.

Train B departure time = 7:50 a.m.

**Concept Used:**

Relative speed concept and distance calculation.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Time difference between Train A and Train B = 50 minutes = 50/60 hours = 5/6 hours

Distance covered by Train A in 5/6 hours = 80 km/h × 5/6 hours

⇒ Distance covered by Train A = 80 × 5/6 km

⇒ Distance covered by Train A = 400/6 km

Relative speed of Train B with respect to Train A = 100 km/h - 80 km/h

⇒ Relative speed = 20 km/h

Time taken for Train B to catch up Train A = Distance / Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = (400/6) km / 20 km/h = 10/3 hours

Distance traveled by Train B in (10/3) hours = 100 km/h × (10/3) hours

⇒ Distance traveled by Train B = 100 × (10/3) = 1000/3 km

Thus, the distance from Delhi where the two trains meet is:

⇒ Distance = 1000/3 km

**∴ The two trains will be together after 1000/3 km from Delhi.**
